Wikipedia leaves the snippet to search.

HSTS is preloaded, security.txt is published, and articles read without JavaScript. But the Main Page and the other 18 pages analyzed have no meta description, so search engines pick the snippet.

The lesson for every team: Write a description of about 150 characters for each key page, so you choose the pitch, not the crawler.

Mozilla: 85 languages, no sitemap.

The home page lists 85 hreflang alternates, HSTS is on, and framing is denied. But robots.txt names no sitemap and /sitemap.xml answers 404, so crawlers find pages only by following links.

The lesson for every team: Publish a sitemap.xml of the pages you want found and name it in robots.txt with one Sitemap: line.

DW blocks framing. It skips nosniff.

frame-ancestors 'none' stops other sites from framing it, HSTS is on, and every page analyzed has a canonical. But X-Content-Type-Options is missing on all 20 pages analyzed, so browsers may guess file types.

The lesson for every team: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response. One header stops browsers running a file as the wrong type.

Le Monde has a CSP that allows any https.

A year of HSTS, framing limited to its own origin, and NewsMediaOrganization JSON-LD. Its content security policy exists, but default-src allows any https: source plus 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'.

The lesson for every team: List the script hosts you actually use, then drop 'unsafe-eval'. A policy that allows everything blocks nothing.
